log: Working out who would actually buy this
Discovering candidates and exact source URLs (stage 1 of 2)
Fetching up to 10 exact URLs; validating against at most 48,000 characters
Evaluating candidates against 9 fetched pages (stage 2 of 2)

Coverage gaps. First, no direct first-person buyer voice was retrieved for the two existing GA4-comparison segments: Reddit and community-forum searches were repeatedly answered with vendor pages, directories and aggregator comparisons rather than threads, so segments 1 and 3 still rest on practitioner analyses and one ecommerce forum thread rather than on in-house or agency testimony. Second, no verification of the named enterprise/public-sector logos (GOV.UK, Scottish Government, Bank of England, Bloomberg, Michelin) was attempted or obtained — treat them as unverified logo lists. Third, searches for negative reviews or churn stories about this specific product returned only aggregate ratings, so the seat-pricing and badge objections remain inferred from the vendor's own published terms rather than from a complaining customer. Fourth, searched-and-failed: university/library DPIA decision write-ups, and open-source maintainer threads choosing a privacy analytics vendor for docs sites (results surfaced telemetry debates and GA plugin issues, not a buying decision). Fifth, geography was unspecified in scope, so both EU and US candidates are returned; if the brief is EU-only, the healthcare candidate should be dropped rather than softened, since its disqualifiers (no BAA, EU-only residency) are structural. Finally, the search tool returns summarised page content, so quoted figures should be re-read against the fetched source URLs before any of them appear in copy — particularly the municipal scan percentages and the ~40% Shopify session drop, which are the two numbers doing the most work here.
